title.zh: 新唐書卷七十三 表第十三上 宰相世系三上

translations.literal: The Liu clan derives from the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Liu clan traces its origin to the house of Ji.

sentences.zh: 魯孝公子夷伯展孫無駭生禽，字季，為魯士師，謚曰惠，食采於柳下，遂姓柳氏。

translations.literal: The son of Duke Xiao of Lu, Prince Yibo Zhan, had a grandson Wuhai who fathered Qin, styled Ji, who was Grand Master of Lu, was posthumously titled Hui, received a fief at Liuxia, and thereupon took the surname Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xiao of Lu's son Prince Yibo Zhan was succeeded by his grandson Wuhai, who had a son Qin, styled Ji. Qin served Lu as Grand Master, was posthumously called Hui, held the fief of Liuxia, and his descendants took the surname Liu.

translations.literal: When Chu destroyed Lu, they entered the service of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: After Chu conquered Lu, the clan entered Chu's service.

sentences.zh: 秦幷天下，柳氏遷於河東。

translations.literal: When Qin united the realm, the Liu clan moved to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin unified the empire, the Liu clan relocated to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 秦末，柳下惠裔孫安，始居解縣。

translations.literal: At the end of Qin, An, a descendant of Liuxia Hui, first settled in Jie County.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing days of Qin, An, a descendant of Liuxia Hui, first made his home in Jie County.

translations.literal: An's grandson Wei was Chancellor of Qi under Han.
translations.idiomatic: An's grandson Wei served Han as Chancellor of Qi.

translations.literal: A sixth-generation descendant, Feng, was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness in Later Han.
translations.idiomatic: Six generations later, Feng was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness under the Later Han.

translations.literal: A sixth-generation descendant, Gui, was Director of the Bureau of Personnel in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Six generations later, Gui was Director of the Bureau of Personnel in Jin.

translations.literal: He fathered Jingyou, a Palace Attendant in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingyou was a Palace Attendant in Jin.

translations.literal: Two sons: Qi and Chun.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Qi and Chun.

translations.literal: Qi was an Administrator and was styled the "Western Branch."
translations.idiomatic: Qi served as Administrator; his line was called the "Western Branch."

translations.literal: Qi had two sons: Gong and Qu.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had two sons, Gong and Qu.

sentences.zh: 恭，後魏河東郡守，南徙汝、潁，遂仕江表。

translations.literal: Gong was Administrator of Hedong Commandery in Later Wei, moved south to Ru and Ying, and then entered service south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Gong was Administrator of Hedong in Later Wei, moved south to the Ru and Ying region, and entered service in the lands south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 曾孫緝，宋州別駕、宋安郡守。

translations.literal: A great-grandson, Ji, was Vice-Governor of Song Province and Administrator of Song'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Ji was Vice-Governor of Song Province and Administrator of Song'an Commandery.

sentences.zh: 生僧習，與豫州刺史裴叔業據州歸于後魏，為揚州大中正、尚書右丞、方輿公。

translations.literal: He fathered Sengxi, who, with Inspector of Yuzhou Pei Shuye, held the province and submitted to Later Wei, becoming Superior Locality Assessor of Yangzhou, Vice Director of the Right in the Imperial Secretariat, and Duke of Fangyu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sengxi joined Inspector of Yuzhou Pei Shuye in holding the province and submitting it to Later Wei, then served as Superior Locality Assessor of Yangzhou, Vice Director of the Right in the Imperial Secretariat, and Duke of Fangyu.

translations.literal: Five sons: Zhuo, Qing, Qiu, Gui, and Nie.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: Zhuo, Qing, Qiu, Gui, and Nie.

sentences.zh: 晉太常卿、平陽太守純六世孫懿，後魏車騎大將軍、汾州刺史。

translations.literal: A sixth-generation descendant of Chun, Grand Master of Ceremonies in Jin and Administrator of Pingyang, Yi was General of Chariots and Cavalry in Later Wei and Inspector of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Six generations after Chun—who had been Grand Master of Ceremonies in Jin and Administrator of Pingyang—Yi became General of Chariots and Cavalry in Later Wei and Inspector of Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 生敏，字白澤，隋上大將軍、武德郡公。

translations.literal: He fathered Min, styled Baize, a Senior General in Sui and Duke of Wude Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Min, styled Baize, was a Senior General under Sui and Duke of Wude Commandery.

translations.literal: A collateral cousin, Daomao.
translations.idiomatic: A collateral cousin was Daomao.

sentences.zh: 平陽太守純生卓，晉永嘉中自本郡遷於襄陽，官至汝南太守。

translations.literal: Chun, Administrator of Pingyang, fathered Zhuo, who in the Yongjia era of Jin moved from his native commandery to Xiangyang and rose to Administrator of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Chun, Administrator of Pingyang, had a son Zhuo who during Jin's Yongjia era moved from Pingyang to Xiangyang and eventually became Administrator of Runan.

translations.literal: Four sons: Fu, Tian, Jie, and Fen, styled the "Eastern Branch."
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons—Fu, Tian, Jie, and Fen—whose line was called the "Eastern Branch."

translations.literal: Three chancellors of the Liu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Three members of the Liu clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Shi, Can, and Hun.
translations.idiomatic: They were Shi, Can, and Hun.

translations.literal: The Han clan derives from the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Han clan traces its origin to the house of Ji.

sentences.zh: 晉穆侯㵒少子曲沃桓叔成師生武子萬，食采韓原，生定伯，定伯生子輿，子輿生獻子厥，從封，遂為韓氏。

translations.literal: Duke Mu Bo of Jin's younger son, Cheng Shi, Huan Shu of Quwo, fathered Wan, styled Wuzi, received a fief at Hanyuan, fathered Dingbo, Dingbo fathered Ziyu, Ziyu fathered Xianzi Jue, who received a secondary enfeoffment and thereupon became the Han clan.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Mu Bo of Jin's younger son Cheng Shi, Huan Shu of Quwo, had a son Wan, styled Wuzi, who held the fief of Hanyuan. Wan's line ran through Dingbo and Ziyu to Xianzi Jue, who received a secondary enfeoffment and established the Han clan.

sentences.zh: 十五世孫襄王倉，為秦所滅。

translations.literal: A fifteenth-generation descendant, King Xiang Cang, was destroyed by Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen generations later, King Xiang Cang was overthrown by Qin.

sentences.zh: 少子蟣虱，生信，漢封韓王。

translations.literal: A younger son, Jijishi, fathered Xin, who was enfeoffed as King of Han under Han.
translations.idiomatic: A younger son Jijishi had a son Xin, who was enfeoffed as King of Han under the Han dynasty.

translations.literal: He fathered Tuidang, Marquis of Gonggao.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tuidang was Marquis of Gonggao.

translations.literal: Tuidang fathered Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Tuidang's son was Ru.

translations.literal: Ru fathered Shuo, Marquis of Andaodao.
translations.idiomatic: Ru's son Shuo was Marquis of Andaodao.

translations.literal: Shuo fathered Changjun.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo's son was Changjun.

translations.literal: Changjun fathered Zeng, Marquis of Long'e.
translations.idiomatic: Changjun's son Zeng was Marquis of Long'e.

sentences.zh: 增生河南尹騫，避王莽亂，居赭陽。

translations.literal: Zeng fathered Qian, Intendant of Henan, who, fleeing Wang Mang's turmoil, settled at Zheyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng's son Qian, Intendant of Henan, fled Wang Mang's rebellion and settled at Zheyang.

sentences.zh: 九世孫河東太守術，生河東太守純。

translations.literal: A ninth-generation descendant, Shu, Administrator of Hedong, fathered Chun, Administrator of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Nine generations later, Shu, Administrator of Hedong, had a son Chun, also Administrator of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 純生魏司徒南鄉恭侯暨。

translations.literal: Chun fathered Ji, Chancellor of State in Wei and Marquis Gong of Nanxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's son Ji was Chancellor of State in Wei and Marquis Gong of Nanxiang.

sentences.zh: 六世孫延之，字顯宗，後魏魯陽侯。

translations.literal: A sixth-generation descendant, Yanzhi, styled Xianzong, was Marquis of Luoyang in Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Six generations later, Yanzhi, styled Xianzong, was Marquis of Luoyang in Later Wei.

translations.literal: His grandson Gui was Administrator of Pingliang and Duke of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Gui was Administrator of Pingliang and Duke of Anding.

translations.literal: He fathered Yan, Inspector of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan was Inspector of Hengzhou.

translations.literal: Yan fathered Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's son was Bao.

sentences.zh: 弓高侯頹當裔孫尋，後漢隴西太守，世居潁川，生司空稜，字伯師，其後徙安定武安。

translations.literal: A descendant of Tuidang, Marquis of Gonggao, Xun was Administrator of Longxi in Later Han; the clan dwelt for generations in Yingchuan; he fathered Ling, styled Boshi, Minister of Works, and afterward they moved to Wu'an in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, a descendant of Tuidang, Marquis of Gonggao, was Administrator of Longxi under the Later Han; the clan long lived in Yingchuan. He had a son Ling, styled Boshi, who was Minister of Works, and later the line moved to Wu'an in Anding.

sentences.zh: 後魏有常山太守、武安成侯耆，字黃耇，徙居九門。

translations.literal: In Later Wei there was Qi, Administrator of Changshan and Marquis Cheng of Wu'an, styled Huangjiu, who moved to Jiumen.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Wei, Qi, styled Huangjiu, was Administrator of Changshan and Marquis Cheng of Wu'an; he relocated to Jiumen.

sentences.zh: 生茂，字元興，尚書令、征南大將軍、安定桓王。

translations.literal: He fathered Mao, styled Yuanxing, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, General Who Conquers the South, and Prince Huan of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mao, styled Yuanxing, was Director of the Imperial Secretariat, General Who Conquers the South, and Prince Huan of Anding.

translations.literal: Two sons: Bei and Jun.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Bei and Jun.

sentences.zh: 均字天德，定州刺史、安定康公。

translations.literal: Jun, styled Tiande, was Inspector of Dingzhou and Duke Kang of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, styled Tiande, was Inspector of Dingzhou and Duke Kang of Anding.

translations.literal: He fathered Jun, Regional Commander of Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jun was Regional Commander of Yazhou.

translations.literal: He fathered Rentai.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Rentai.

sentences.zh: 河東太守純四世孫安之，晉員外郎。

translations.literal: A fourth-generation descendant of Chun, Administrator of Hedong, Anzhi was an Attendant Officer Outside the Staff in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Four generations after Chun, Administrator of Hedong, came Anzhi, an Attendant Officer Outside the Staff in Jin.

translations.literal: Two sons: Qian and Tian.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Qian and Tian.

translations.literal: Tian was Administrator of Xuantu.
translations.idiomatic: Tian served as Administrator of Xuantu.

translations.literal: Two sons: Du and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Du and Yan.

sentences.zh: 偃，臨江令，生後魏從事郎中穎。

translations.literal: Yan was Magistrate of Linjiang; he fathered Ying, a Staff Officer of the Attendant in Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was Magistrate of Linjiang and had a son Ying, a Staff Officer of the Attendant in Later Wei.

sentences.zh: 穎生播，字遠游，徙昌黎棘城。

translations.literal: Ying fathered Bo, styled Yuanyou, who moved to Jicheng in Changli.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's son Bo, styled Yuanyou, relocated to Jicheng in Changli.

translations.literal: Two sons: Li and Shao.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Li and Shao.

translations.literal: Shao, styled Yanzong, was Vice-Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shao, styled Yanzong, was Vice-Governor of Yangzhou.

translations.literal: Two sons: Yi and Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Yi and Zhou.

sentences.zh: 南鄉恭侯暨子孫其後徙陽夏。

translations.literal: The descendants of Marquis Gong of Nanxiang, Ji, afterward moved to Yangxia.
translations.idiomatic: The descendants of Marquis Gong of Nanxiang, Ji, later relocated to Yangxia.

translations.literal: Four chancellors of the Han clan.
translations.idiomatic: Four members of the Han clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Yuan, Xiu, Huang, and Hong.
translations.idiomatic: They were Yuan, Xiu, Huang, and Hong.

translations.literal: The Lai clan derives from the Zi surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Lai clan traces its origin to the house of Zi.

sentences.zh: 商之支孫食采於郲，因以為氏，其後避難去「邑」。

translations.literal: A collateral branch of the Shang house held a fief at Lai and took that place as their clan name; later, to escape turmoil, they dropped the "city" radical from the character.
translations.idiomatic: A collateral branch of the Shang house held a fief at Lai and took that place as their clan name; later, to escape turmoil, they dropped the "city" radical from the character.

translations.literal: At the end of Qin they moved to Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing days of Qin the clan relocated to Xinye.

sentences.zh: 漢有光祿大夫來漢，從楊僕擊南越。

translations.literal: Under Han there was Lai Han, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, who followed Yang Pu in attacking Nanyue.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times Lai Han was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and campaigned against Nanyue under Yang Pu.

translations.literal: His grandson Zhong was Grand Master of Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Zhong was Grand Master of Remonstrance.

translations.literal: He fathered She, styled Junshu, General of the Gentlemen of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: His son She, styled Junshu, was General of the Gentlemen of the Household.

translations.literal: He fathered Ling.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Ling.

translations.literal: Ling fathered Li, who served as Commandant of the Bearer of the Mace.
translations.idiomatic: Ling's son Li was Commandant of the Bearer of the Mace.

translations.literal: He fathered Ding, General of the Gentlemen of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ding was General of the Gentlemen of the Household.

translations.literal: His grandson Yan was Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yan was Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 生敏，字敬達，蜀執慎將軍。

translations.literal: He fathered Min, styled Jingda, General Who Maintains Vigilance in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Min, styled Jingda, was General Who Maintains Vigilance in Shu.

translations.literal: A seventh-generation descendant, Ce, first moved to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Seven generations later, Ce first relocated the clan to Jiangdu.

translations.literal: Two chancellors of the Lai clan.
translations.idiomatic: Two members of the Lai clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Ji and Heng.
translations.idiomatic: They were Ji and Heng.

translations.literal: The Xu clan derives from the Jiang surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Xu clan traces its origin to the house of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 炎帝裔孫伯夷之後，周武王封其裔孫文叔於許，後以為太嶽之嗣，至元公結為楚所滅，遷于容城，子孫分散，以國為氏。

translations.literal: Descendants of Boyi, a collateral descendant of the Yan Emperor; King Wu of Zhou enfeoffed his descendant Wenshu at Xu; afterward he was made heir to Taiyue; when Duke Yuan Jie was destroyed by Chu, they moved to Rongcheng, descendants dispersed, and took the state as their surname.
translations.idiomatic: From Boyi, a descendant of the Yan Emperor, came Wenshu, whom King Wu of Zhou enfeoffed at Xu; the line later became heirs to Taiyue. When Duke Yuan Jie was destroyed by Chu, the clan moved to Rongcheng; descendants scattered and took the state name as their surname.

sentences.zh: 自容城徙冀州高陽北新城都鄉樂善里。

translations.literal: From Rongcheng they moved to Leshan Village, Duxiang, Xincheng, north of Gaoyang in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: From Rongcheng the clan relocated to Leshan Village in Duxiang, Xincheng, north of Gaoyang in Jizhou.

translations.literal: At the end of Qin there was Xu Yi, who lived in seclusion and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing days of Qin, Xu Yi lived in seclusion and refused office.

translations.literal: A great-grandson, Pi, was a Palace Attendant and Grand Master of Ceremonies in Han.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Pi was a Palace Attendant and Grand Master of Ceremonies under Han.

sentences.zh: 生德，字伯饒，安定、汝南太守，因居平輿。

translations.literal: He fathered De, styled Bora, Administrator of Anding and Runan, and thereby settled at Pingyu.
translations.idiomatic: His son De, styled Bora, served as Administrator of Anding and Runan and made his home at Pingyu.

translations.literal: Four sons: Ju, Zheng, Miao, and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Ju, Zheng, Miao, and Jin.

translations.literal: Ju was Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Ju served as Grand Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 生允，字士崇，魏中領軍、鎮北將軍。

translations.literal: He fathered Yun, styled Shichong, Central Army Commander and General Who Guards the North in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yun, styled Shichong, was Central Army Commander and General Who Guards the North in Wei.

translations.literal: Three sons: Yin, Dong, and Meng.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Yin, Dong, and Meng.

translations.literal: Yun's grandson Shi; Shi had two sons: Fan and Mai.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's grandson Shi had two sons, Fan and Mai.

translations.literal: Fan, styled Zhongren, was a clerk to the Chancellor of State in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Fan, styled Zhongren, was clerk to the Chancellor of State in Jin.

translations.literal: Four sons: Mao, Xun, Ni, and Ya.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Mao, Xun, Ni, and Ya.

sentences.zh: 詢字玄度，四子：元之、仲之、季之、珪。

translations.literal: Xun, styled Xuandu, had four sons: Yuanzhi, Zhongzhi, Jizhi, and Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, styled Xuandu, had four sons: Yuanzhi, Zhongzhi, Jizhi, and Gui.

sentences.zh: 珪，宋給事、著作郎、桂陽太守。

translations.literal: Gui was a Secretary in Attendance, Author at the Archive, and Administrator of Guiyang in Song.
translations.idiomatic: Gui served Song as Secretary in Attendance, Author at the Archive, and Administrator of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 生勇慧，齊太子家令、宂從僕射、晉陵縣侯。

translations.literal: He fathered Yonghui, Chief Steward to the Heir Apparent in Qi, Junior Assistant Master of Ceremonies, and Marquis of Jinling County.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yonghui was Chief Steward to the Heir Apparent in Qi, Junior Assistant Master of Ceremonies, and Marquis of Jinling County.

translations.literal: Two sons: Mao and Yin.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Mao and Yin.

sentences.zh: 懋，梁天門太守、中庶子，生亨。

translations.literal: Mao was Administrator of Tianmen and Junior Tutor in Liang; he fathered Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Mao was Administrator of Tianmen and Junior Tutor under Liang and had a son Heng.

sentences.zh: 德次子政，字義先，別居邵陵。

translations.literal: De's second son Zheng, styled Yixian, separately settled at Shaoling.
translations.idiomatic: De's second son Zheng, styled Yixian, established a separate branch at Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 安陸許氏出自詢五世孫君明，梁楚州刺吏，生弘周。

translations.literal: The Anlu Xu clan derives from Junming, a fifth-generation descendant of Xun, Inspector of Chuzhou in Liang; he fathered Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Anlu branch of the Xu clan descended from Junming, five generations after Xun; Junming was Inspector of Chuzhou in Liang and had a son Hongzhou.

translations.literal: Two chancellors of the Xu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Two members of the Xu clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Jingzong and Yushi.
translations.idiomatic: They were Jingzong and Yushi.

translations.literal: The Xin clan derives from the Si surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Xin clan traces its origin to the house of Si.

sentences.zh: 夏后啟封支子於莘，「莘」「辛」聲相近，遂為辛氏。

translations.literal: Xia Hou Qi enfeoffed a collateral son at Shen; since "Shen" and "Xin" are close in sound, they thereupon became the Xin clan.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Hou Qi enfeoffed a collateral son at Shen; because "Shen" and "Xin" are similar in pronunciation, the clan became the Xin house.

sentences.zh: 周太史辛甲為文王臣，封於長子。

translations.literal: Xin Jia, Grand Historian of Zhou, served King Wen as a minister and was enfeoffed at Changzi.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Jia, Grand Historian of Zhou, served King Wen as a minister and was enfeoffed at Changzi.

sentences.zh: 秦有將軍辛騰，家于中山苦陘。

translations.literal: In Qin there was the general Xin Teng, whose family made their home at Kusui in Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qin the general Xin Teng had his family seat at Kusui in Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 曾孫蒲，漢初以豪族徙隴西狄道。

translations.literal: A great-grandson, Pu, was relocated in early Han as a powerful clan to Didao in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Pu was relocated in early Han to Didao in Longxi as a prominent clan.

sentences.zh: 曾孫柔，字長汎，光祿大夫、右扶風都尉、馮翊太守。

translations.literal: A great-grandson, Rou, styled Changfan, was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Commandant of Right Fufeng, and Administrator of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Rou, styled Changfan, was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Commandant of Right Fufeng, and Administrator of Fengyi.

translations.literal: Four sons: Lin, Zhong, Wuxian, and Dengweng.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Lin, Zhong, Wuxian, and Dengweng.

translations.literal: Wuxian was General Who Subdues the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxian served as General Who Subdues the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 生慶忌，左將軍、光祿大夫、常樂公。

translations.literal: He fathered Qingji, Left General, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and Duke of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qingji was Left General, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and Duke of Changle.

translations.literal: He fathered Zichan, Administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zichan became Administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 曾孫茂，後漢成義將軍、酒泉太守、侍中。

translations.literal: A great-grandson, Mao, was General of Accomplished Righteousness in Later Han, Administrator of Jiuquan, and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Mao was General of Accomplished Righteousness under the Later Han, Administrator of Jiuquan, and a Palace Attendant.

translations.literal: Three sons: Jian, Shu, and Mengsun.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Jian, Shu, and Mengsun.

translations.literal: Mengsun fathered Bozhen, Commandant of the Chang River.
translations.idiomatic: Mengsun's son Bozhen was Commandant of the Chang River.

translations.literal: Bozhen had two sons: Mengxing and Shuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhen had two sons, Mengxing and Shuxing.

translations.literal: Mengxing had two sons: En and Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxing had two sons, En and Yin.

translations.literal: En fathered Ziyan.
translations.idiomatic: En's son was Ziyan.

translations.literal: Ziyan had three sons: Yin, Yu, and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyan had three sons: Yin, Yu, and Xu.

translations.literal: One chancellor of the Xin clan.
translations.idiomatic: One member of the Xin clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Mao Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was Mao Jiang.

sentences.zh: 任任姓出自黃帝少子禹陽，受封於任，因以為姓。

translations.literal: The Ren surname derives from Shaozi Yuyang of the Yellow Emperor, who received a fief at Ren and thereupon took it as a surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Ren clan traces its origin to Yuyang, a son of the Yellow Emperor, who was enfeoffed at Ren and took that place as his surname.

sentences.zh: 十二世孫奚仲，為夏車正，更封於薛。

translations.literal: A twelfth-generation descendant, Xizhong, was Master of Chariots in Xia and was enfeoffed again at Xue.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve generations later, Xizhong became Master of Chariots under Xia and was enfeoffed anew at Xue.

sentences.zh: 又十二世孫仲虺，為湯左相。

translations.literal: Another twelfth-generation descendant, Zhonghui, was Left Chancellor to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Another twelve generations on, Zhonghui served Tang as Left Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 太戊時有臣扈，武丁時有祖巳，皆徙國於邳。

translations.literal: In the time of Tai Wu there was the minister Hu; in the time of Wu Ding there was Zusi—both moved their states to Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tai Wu there was the minister Hu; under Wu Ding there was Zusi—each relocated the state to Pi.

sentences.zh: 祖巳七世孫成侯，又遷於摯，亦謂之摯國。

translations.literal: A seventh-generation descendant of Zusi, Marquis Cheng, moved again to Zhi, which was also called the state of Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Seven generations after Zusi, Marquis Cheng moved the line again to Zhi, also known as the state of Zhi.

sentences.zh: 漢有御史大夫廣阿侯任敖，世居于沛，其後徙居渭南。

translations.literal: Under Han there was Ren Ao, Grand Censor and Marquis of Guang'a, whose family dwelt for generations in Pei and later moved to Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times Ren Ao was Grand Censor and Marquis of Guang'a; the clan long lived in Pei before moving to Weinan.

translations.literal: One chancellor of the Ren clan.
translations.idiomatic: One member of the Ren clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Yaxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was Yaxiang.

translations.literal: The Lu clan derives from the Jiang surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Lu clan traces its origin to the house of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 齊文公子高，高孫傒為齊正卿，謚曰敬仲，食采於盧，濟北盧縣是也，其後因以為氏。

translations.literal: The son of Duke Wen of Qi, Gao, had a grandson Xi who was Chief Minister of Qi, was posthumously titled Jingzhong, received a fief at Lu—that is Lu County in Jibei—and the descendants thereupon took it as a surname.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen of Qi's son Gao was succeeded by his grandson Xi, Chief Minister of Qi. Posthumously called Jingzhong, he held the fief of Lu in Jibei, and his descendants took that place as their surname.

sentences.zh: 田和篡齊，盧氏散居燕、秦之間。

translations.literal: When Tian He usurped Qi, the Lu clan scattered between Yan and Qin.
translations.idiomatic: After Tian He seized Qi, the Lu clan dispersed between Yan and Qin.

sentences.zh: 秦有博士敖，子孫家于涿水之上，遂為范陽涿人。

translations.literal: In Qin there was the Erudite Ao, whose descendants made their home above the Zhuo River and thus became natives of Zhuo in Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qin the Erudite Ao had descendants who settled above the Zhuo River and became the Zhuo branch of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 裔孫植，字子幹，漢北中郎將。

translations.literal: A descendant, Zhi, styled Zigàn, was a General of the Northern Gentlemen of the Household in Han.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant Zhi, styled Zigàn, was Han's General of the Northern Gentlemen of the Household.

sentences.zh: 生毓，字子象，魏司空、容城成侯。

translations.literal: He fathered Yu, styled Zixiang, Chancellor of State in Wei and Marquis Cheng of Rongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu, styled Zixiang, was Chancellor of State in Wei and Marquis Cheng of Rongcheng.

translations.literal: Three sons: Qin, Jian, and Ting.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Qin, Jian, and Ting.

translations.literal: Qin was Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Qin served Jin as Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 珽字子笏，晉侍中尚書、廣燕穆子。

translations.literal: Ting, styled Zihu, was a Palace Attendant and Director of the Imperial Secretariat in Jin and Prince Mu of Guangyan.
translations.idiomatic: Ting, styled Zihu, was Jin's Palace Attendant and Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Prince Mu of Guangyan.

translations.literal: Three sons: Fu, Hao, and Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Fu, Hao, and Zhi.

sentences.zh: 志字子道，晉中書監、衞尉卿。

translations.literal: Zhi, styled Zidao, was Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Commandant of the Guards in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, styled Zidao, was Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Commandant of the Guards under Jin.

translations.literal: Three sons: Chen, Mi, and Shen.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Chen, Mi, and Shen.

sentences.zh: 諶字子諒，晉侍中、中書監。

translations.literal: Chen, styled Ziliang, was a Palace Attendant and Director of the Imperial Secretariat in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, styled Ziliang, was a Palace Attendant and Director of the Imperial Secretariat in Jin.

translations.literal: Five sons: Xu, Ning, Rong, Yan, and Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: Xu, Ning, Rong, Yan, and Zheng.

translations.literal: Xu dwelt south of the lane and was styled the "Southern Ancestor."
translations.idiomatic: Xu lived south of the lane and his branch was called the "Southern Ancestor."

translations.literal: Yan dwelt to the north and was styled the "Northern Ancestor."
translations.idiomatic: Yan lived to the north and his branch was called the "Northern Ancestor."

translations.literal: Yan served the Murong clan as Administrator of Yingqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Yan entered the service of the Murong and became Administrator of Yingqiu.

translations.literal: Two sons: Miao and Chan.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Miao and Chan.

translations.literal: Miao was Administrator of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Miao became Administrator of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 生玄，字子真，後魏中書侍郎、固安宣侯。

translations.literal: He fathered Xuan, styled Zizhen, Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat in Later Wei and Marquis Xuan of Guo'an.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuan, styled Zizhen, was Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat in Later Wei and Marquis Xuan of Guo'an.

translations.literal: Two sons: Xun and Dushi.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Xun and Dushi.

sentences.zh: 度世字子遷，青州刺史固安惠侯。

translations.literal: Dushi, styled Ziqian, was Inspector of Qingzhou and Marquis Hui of Guo'an.
translations.idiomatic: Dushi, styled Ziqian, was Inspector of Qingzhou and Marquis Hui of Guo'an.

sentences.zh: 四子：陽烏、敏、昶、尚之，號「四房盧氏」。

translations.literal: Four sons: Yangwu, Min, Chang, and Shangzhi, styled the "Four Houses of the Lu Clan."
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons—Yangwu, Min, Chang, and Shangzhi—and their lines were known as the "Four Houses of the Lu Clan."

translations.literal: The Fanyang Lu clan also had Lu Sun.
translations.idiomatic: The Fanyang branch of the Lu clan also included Lu Sun.

translations.literal: Eight chancellors of the Lu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Eight members of the Lu clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: The senior house had Shang and Chengqing;
translations.idiomatic: The senior house produced Shang and Chengqing;

translations.literal: the second house had Han and Mai;
translations.idiomatic: the second house produced Han and Mai;

translations.literal: the third house had Huai Shen and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: the third house produced Huai Shen and Qi.

translations.literal: In Fanyang there were Kai and Guangqi.
translations.idiomatic: In Fanyang there were Kai and Guangqi.

translations.literal: The Shangguan clan derives from the Mi surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Shangguan clan traces its origin to the house of Mi.

sentences.zh: 楚王子蘭為上官大夫，以族為氏。

translations.literal: The Chu prince Zilan served as Grand Master Shangguan, and the clan took his office as their surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Chu prince Zilan was Grand Master Shangguan, and the clan took that title as their surname.

sentences.zh: 漢徙大姓以實關中，上官氏徙隴西上邽。

translations.literal: Han moved great clans to populate Guanzhong, and the Shangguan clan was relocated to Shanggui in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Han settled great families in Guanzhong, the Shangguan clan was moved to Shanggui in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 漢有右將軍安陽侯桀，生安，車騎將軍、桑樂侯，以反伏誅。

translations.literal: Under Han there was Jie, General of the Right and Marquis of Anyang, who fathered An, General of Chariots and Cavalry and Marquis of Sangle, who was executed for rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times Jie was General of the Right and Marquis of Anyang; his son An was General of Chariots and Cavalry and Marquis of Sangle, and was put to death for rebellion.

sentences.zh: 遺腹子期，裔孫勝，蜀太尉。

translations.literal: A posthumous son, Qi; a descendant, Sheng, was Grand Commandant of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: A posthumous son Qi survived; a descendant Sheng became Grand Commandant of Shu.

translations.literal: Two sons: styled Mao and styled Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons known as Mao and Xian.

translations.literal: Xian moved to Dong Commandery and later to Shan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Xian branch moved to Dong Commandery and later to Shan Commandery.

translations.literal: A fifth-generation descendant, Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations later came Hui.

sentences.zh: 至弘為江都總監，又徙揚州。

translations.literal: When Hong became Director-General of Jiangdu, they moved again to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong became Director-General of Jiangdu, the clan relocated to Yangzhou.

translations.literal: One chancellor of the Shangguan clan.
translations.idiomatic: One member of the Shangguan clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was Yi.

translations.literal: The Yue clan derives from the Zi surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Yue clan traces its origin to the house of Zi.

sentences.zh: 宋戴公生公子衎，字樂父，生傾父澤，澤生夷父須，子孫以王父字為氏。

translations.literal: Duke Dai of Song fathered the prince Kan, styled Yuefu, who fathered Qingfuzi Ze; Ze fathered Yifuxu; descendants took their great-grandfather's style as their surname.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Dai of Song had a son Kan, styled Yuefu; Kan's son Ze was called Qingfuzi; Ze's son was Yifuxu—and later generations took Yuefu's style as their clan name.

sentences.zh: 須生大司寇樂呂，呂孫喜，喜生司城子罕。

translations.literal: Xu fathered Yuelü, Grand Minister of Works; Yuelü's grandson was Xi; Xi fathered Zihan, Minister of the City.
translations.idiomatic: Yifuxu's son Yuelü became Grand Minister of Works; Yuelü's grandson Xi had a son Zihan, Minister of the City.

sentences.zh: 裔孫樂羊，為魏文侯將，封於靈壽，其後子孫因家焉。

translations.literal: A descendant, Yue Yang, was a general to Marquis Wen of Wei and was enfeoffed at Lingshou; afterward descendants made their home there.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant Yue Yang was a general to Marquis Wen of Wei and was enfeoffed at Lingshou, where the clan later settled.

translations.literal: A descendant, Yi, was enfeoffed in Zhao as Lord of Wangzhu.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant Yi was enfeoffed in Zhao as Lord of Wangzhu.

sentences.zh: 毅孫臣叔，漢封華成君，子孫自趙徙長陵。

translations.literal: Yi's grandson Chenshu was enfeoffed in Han as Lord of Huacheng, and descendants moved from Zhao to Changling.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's grandson Chenshu was enfeoffed as Lord of Huacheng under Han, and the line moved from Zhao to Changling.

translations.literal: A descendant, Qin, was a clerk of the native county in Later Han.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant Qin was a clerk in his home county under the Later Han.

translations.literal: He fathered Hui, styled Boqi, Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui, styled Boqi, became Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 生羽林監乾，徙南陽淯陽。

translations.literal: He fathered Gan, Supervisor of the Feathered Forest, who moved to Yuyang in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gan, Supervisor of the Feathered Forest, relocated the family to Yuyang in Nanyang.

translations.literal: His grandson Ren was Administrator of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Ren was Administrator of Wuling.

translations.literal: He fathered Ping, Administrator of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ping was Administrator of Qinghe.

translations.literal: Ping fathered Fang, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Ping's son Fang was Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 生廣，字彥輔，晉尚書令、信陵公。

translations.literal: He fathered Guang, styled Yanfu, Director of the Imperial Secretariat in Jin and Duke of Xinling.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guang, styled Yanfu, was Director of the Imperial Secretariat in Jin and Duke of Xinling.

translations.literal: A descendant, Xun.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant was Xun.

translations.literal: Two chancellors of the Yue clan.
translations.idiomatic: Two members of the Yue clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Yanwei and Sihui.
translations.idiomatic: They were Yanwei and Sihui.

translations.literal: The Sun clan derives from the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Sun clan traces its origin to the house of Ji.

sentences.zh: 衞康叔八世孫武公和生公子惠孫，惠孫生耳，為衞上卿，食采於戚，生武仲乙，以王父字為氏。

translations.literal: Kang Shu of Wei's eighth-generation descendant Duke Wu He fathered the prince Huisun; Huisun fathered Er, who was Chief Minister of Wei, received a fief at Qi, and fathered Wuzhong Yi, who took his grandfather's style as his surname.
translations.idiomatic: Eight generations after Kang Shu of Wei, Duke Wu He had a son Huisun; Huisun's son Er was Chief Minister of Wei and held the fief of Qi; Er's son Wuzhong Yi took his grandfather's style as the clan name.

sentences.zh: 乙生昭子炎，炎生莊子紇，紇生宣子鰌，鰌生桓子良夫，良夫生文子林父，林父生嘉，世居汲郡。

translations.literal: Yi fathered Zhaozi Yan; Yan fathered Zhuangzi Ge; Ge fathered Xuanzi Kun; Kun fathered Huanzi Liangfu; Liangfu fathered Wenzi Linfu; Linfu fathered Jia, and the line dwelt for generations in Ji Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's line ran through Zhaozi Yan, Zhuangzi Ge, Xuanzi Kun, Huanzi Liangfu, and Wenzi Linfu; Linfu's son Jia made the clan's home in Ji Commandery for generations.

translations.literal: In Jin there was Sun Deng, who was of this descent.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Deng of Jin belonged to this branch.

translations.literal: There was also a line deriving from the Mi surname.
translations.idiomatic: Another branch derived from the house of Mi.

sentences.zh: 楚蚡冒生王子蒍章，字無鉤，生蒍叔伯呂臣，孫蒍賈伯嬴生蒍艾獵，即令尹叔敖，亦為孫氏。

translations.literal: Fenmao of Chu fathered the prince Wanzhang, styled Wugou, who fathered Uncle Lüchen; his grandson Boying Jia fathered Ai Lie, who was Chief Minister Shu Ao and also became the Sun clan.
translations.idiomatic: Chu's Fenmao had a son Wanzhang, styled Wugou; Wanzhang's son was Uncle Lüchen; the grandson Jia of the Ying house fathered Ai Lie—Chief Minister Shu Ao—who also established the Sun line.

translations.literal: There was also a line deriving from the Gui surname.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a branch from the house of Gui.

sentences.zh: 齊田完字敬仲，四世孫桓子無宇，無宇二子：恒、書。

translations.literal: Tian Wan of Qi, styled Jingzhong, had a fourth-generation descendant Huanzi Wuyu; Wuyu had two sons: Heng and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Wan of Qi, styled Jingzhong, was followed four generations later by Huanzi Wuyu, who had two sons: Heng and Shu.

sentences.zh: 書字子占，齊大夫，伐莒有功，景公賜姓孫氏，食采於樂安。

translations.literal: Shu, styled Zizhan, was a grand minister of Qi; for merit in attacking Ju, Duke Jing bestowed the surname Sun and a fief at Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, styled Zizhan, was a grand minister of Qi; for his campaign against Ju, Duke Jing granted the surname Sun and a fief at Le'an.

translations.literal: He fathered Ping, styled Qizong, a minister of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ping, styled Qizong, was a minister of Qi.

sentences.zh: 憑生武，字長卿，以田、鮑四族謀為亂，奔吳，為將軍。

translations.literal: Ping fathered Wu, styled Changqing, who, when the Tian, Bao, and other four clans plotted rebellion, fled to Wu and became a general.
translations.idiomatic: Ping's son Wu, styled Changqing, fled to Wu and became a general when the Tian, Bao, and three other clans plotted rebellion.

translations.literal: Three sons: Chi, Ming, and Di.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Chi, Ming, and Di.

sentences.zh: 明食采於富春，自是世為富春人。

translations.literal: Ming received a fief at Fuchun, and from then on the clan were natives of Fuchun for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Ming held a fief at Fuchun, and thereafter the clan were Fuchun people for generations.

sentences.zh: 明生髕，髕生勝，字國輔，秦將。

translations.literal: Ming fathered Bin; Bin fathered Sheng, styled Guofu, a general of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Ming's son Bin had a son Sheng, styled Guofu, who was a Qin general.

translations.literal: Sheng fathered Gai, styled Guangdao, Administrator of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's son Gai, styled Guangdao, was Administrator of Hanzhong.

translations.literal: He fathered Zhi, styled Wanfang, enfeoffed as Lord of Wuxin.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi, styled Wanfang, was enfeoffed as Lord of Wuxin.

sentences.zh: 知生念，字甚然，二子：豐、益。

translations.literal: Zhi fathered Nian, styled Shenran, who had two sons: Feng and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's son Nian, styled Shenran, had two sons: Feng and Yi.

sentences.zh: 益字玄器，生卿，字伯高，漢侍中。

translations.literal: Yi, styled Xuanqi, fathered Qing, styled Bogao, a Palace Attendant in Han.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, styled Xuanqi, had a son Qing, styled Bogao, who was a Palace Attendant under Han.

translations.literal: He fathered Ping, styled Jingchun, a general.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ping, styled Jingchun, was a general.

translations.literal: Two sons: Jie and Xun.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Jie and Xun.

translations.literal: Xun, styled Huizong, was Administrator of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, styled Huizong, was Administrator of Anding.

translations.literal: Two sons: Luan and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Luan and Qi.

sentences.zh: 鸞生爰居，爰居生福，為太原太守，遇赤眉之難，遂居太原中都。

translations.literal: Luan fathered Aiju; Aiju fathered Fu, who was Administrator of Taiyuan; encountering the Red Eyebrows' turmoil, he then settled at Zhongdu in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Luan's son Aiju had a son Fu, Administrator of Taiyuan; during the Red Eyebrows' uprising he made his home at Zhongdu in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 太原之族有嵐州刺史昉，生存進，安定太守。

translations.literal: Among the Taiyuan branch there was Fang, Inspector of Lanzhou; Fang fathered Shengjin, Administrator of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taiyuan branch was Fang, Inspector of Lanzhou, whose son Shengjin was Administrator of Anding.

sentences.zh: 詢次子騏，字士龍，安邑令。

translations.literal: Xun's second son Qi, styled Shilong, was Magistrate of Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's second son Qi, styled Shilong, was Magistrate of Anyi.

translations.literal: Two sons: Tong and Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Tong and Xiong.

sentences.zh: 通子孫世居清河，後魏有清河太守靈懷。

translations.literal: Tong's descendants dwelt for generations in Qinghe; in Later Wei there was Linghuai, Administrator of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Tong's line settled in Qinghe for generations; in Later Wei Linghuai was Administrator of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 武德中，子孫因官徙汝州郟城。

translations.literal: In the Wude era, descendants moved because of official appointments to Jiacheng in Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wude era the clan relocated to Jiacheng in Ruzhou on account of office.

translations.literal: A great-grandson of Linghuai, Maodao.
translations.idiomatic: Maodao was Linghuai's great-grandson.

sentences.zh: 安邑令騏少子敻，字子遠，後漢天水太守，徙居青州，生厚，字重殷，大將軍掾。

translations.literal: The youngest son of Qi, Magistrate of Anyi, Xiong, styled Ziyuan, was Administrator of Tianshui in Later Han, moved to Qingzhou, and fathered Hou, styled Chongyin, a staff officer to the Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Qi the Magistrate of Anyi had a youngest son Xiong, styled Ziyuan, Administrator of Tianshui under Later Han; he moved to Qingzhou and had a son Hou, styled Chongyin, who was staff officer to the Grand General.

translations.literal: He fathered Yao, styled Liangyu, a General of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yao, styled Liangyu, was a General of the Household.

translations.literal: He fathered Sui, styled Boyuan, Administrator of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sui, styled Boyuan, was Administrator of Qinghe.

translations.literal: He fathered Shu, styled Shiyan, Magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shu, styled Shiyan, was Magistrate of Luoyang.

translations.literal: He fathered Guo, styled Mingyuan, a Gentleman of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guo, styled Mingyuan, was a Gentleman of the Imperial Secretariat.

translations.literal: He fathered Dan, styled Xuanzhi, Administrator of Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dan, styled Xuanzhi, was Administrator of Hanyang.

translations.literal: Two sons: Zhong and Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Zhong and Zhan.

translations.literal: Zhong: Wu's founding ruler Quan was of this descent.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhong's line came Sun Quan, founding ruler of Wu.

translations.literal: Zhan, styled Zizhi, was Administrator of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan, styled Zizhi, was Administrator of Taiyuan.

translations.literal: Two sons: Yan and Li.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Yan and Li.

translations.literal: Yan, styled Shuran, was Director of the Imperial Library in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, styled Shuran, was Director of the Imperial Library under Wei.

translations.literal: He fathered Leng, styled Zhonggu, Grand Provisioner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Leng, styled Zhonggu, was Grand Provisioner.

sentences.zh: 生道恭，字雅遜，晉長秋卿。

translations.literal: He fathered Daogong, styled Yasun, Director of the Palace Domestic Service in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daogong, styled Yasun, was Director of the Palace Domestic Service in Jin.

translations.literal: Two sons: Yi and Fang.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Yi and Fang.

translations.literal: Yi, styled Shiruo.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was styled Shiruo.

translations.literal: Fang was Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子烈，避趙王倫之難，徙居昌黎。

translations.literal: His son Lie, fleeing the turmoil of Prince Lun of Zhao, moved to Changli.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lie fled the crisis of Prince Lun of Zhao and settled in Changli.

sentences.zh: 生岳，前燕侍中，子孫稱昌黎孫氏，歷幽州刺史、右將軍。

translations.literal: He fathered Yue, a Palace Attendant of Former Yan; descendants were styled the Sun clan of Changli; he served successively as Inspector of Youzhou and General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yue was a Palace Attendant of Former Yan; the line came to be called the Sun clan of Changli and held the posts of Inspector of Youzhou and General of the Right.

sentences.zh: 生旂，字伯旗，平南將軍，坐與孫秀合謀，夷三族。

translations.literal: He fathered Qi, styled Boqi, General Who Pacifies the South; because he joined Sun Xiu in conspiracy, three generations of his clan were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qi, styled Boqi, was General Who Pacifies the South; for conspiring with Sun Xiu, three generations of the clan were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 顗避地河朔，居武邑武遂。

translations.literal: Yi fled to the lands north of the Yellow River and settled at Wusui in Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yi took refuge north of the Yellow River and made his home at Wusui in Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 生煇，字光休，後趙射聲校尉。

translations.literal: He fathered Hui, styled Guangxiu, Colonel of the Bowmen in Later Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui, styled Guangxiu, was Colonel of the Bowmen under Later Zhao.

translations.literal: He fathered Wei, styled Yuanwen, Area Commander of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wei, styled Yuanwen, was Area Commander of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 生周，字季洽，後燕高陽王文學。

translations.literal: He fathered Zhou, styled Jiqia, Literary Scholar to Prince Wen of Gaoyang in Later Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhou, styled Jiqia, was Literary Scholar to Prince Wen of Gaoyang under Later Yan.

sentences.zh: 生敬仁，字士和，北燕司隸功曹。

translations.literal: He fathered Jingren, styled Shihe, a Records Officer of the Metropolitan Region in Northern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingren, styled Shihe, was a Records Officer of the Metropolitan Region in Northern Yan.

translations.literal: Two sons: Yuan and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Yuan and Wei.

sentences.zh: 蔚字伯華，一字叔炳，後魏祕書監、棗彊戴男。

translations.literal: Wei, styled Bohua and also styled Shubing, was Director of the Imperial Library in Later Wei and Baron Dai of Zaoqiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, styled Bohua (also Shubing), was Director of the Imperial Library in Later Wei and Baron Dai of Zaoqiang.

translations.literal: Two sons: Boli and Fangsi.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Boli and Fangsi.

translations.literal: Two chancellors of the Sun clan.
translations.idiomatic: Two members of the Sun clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: In Qinghe there was Maodao.
translations.idiomatic: In Qinghe there was Maodao.

translations.literal: In Wuyi there was Wo.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuyi there was Wo.

sentences.zh: 姜姜姓本炎帝，生於姜水，因以為姓。

translations.literal: The Jiang clan: the Jiang surname originally derives from the Flame Emperor; born at the Jiang River, they thereupon took it as their surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang clan originally descended from the Flame Emperor; born beside the Jiang River, they took that river's name as their surname.

translations.literal: Later descendants changed to other surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations adopted other surnames.

sentences.zh: 堯遭洪水，共工之從孫佐禹治水，為四嶽之官，以其主四嶽之祭，尊之，故稱曰「大嶽」，命為侯伯，復賜以祖姓曰姜，以紹炎帝之後。

translations.literal: When Yao suffered the flood, a descendant of Gonggong assisted Yu in controlling the waters, served as one of the Four Peaks' officers, and because he presided over the sacrifices to the Four Peaks and was honored, was styled "Grand Peak"; he was appointed a feudal lord and was again bestowed his ancestral surname Jiang to continue the line of the Flame Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: During Yao's great flood, a descendant of Gonggong assisted Yu in controlling the waters and held office among the Four Peaks; because he presided over their rites he was honored as "Grand Peak," was made a feudal lord, and received the ancestral surname Jiang to carry on the Flame Emperor's line.

sentences.zh: 裔孫太公望封齊，為田和所滅，子孫分散。

translations.literal: A descendant, Grand Duke Wang, was enfeoffed with Qi, was destroyed by Tian He, and descendants scattered.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant, Grand Duke Wang, received Qi as his fief, but Tian He destroyed the state and the clan dispersed.

sentences.zh: 漢初，姜氏以關東大族徙關中，遂居天水。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, the Jiang clan, as a great family east of the Pass, was moved to Guanzhong and thereupon settled in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Han the Jiang clan, a great eastern family, was relocated to Guanzhong and settled in Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 蜀大將軍平襄侯維，裔孫明，世居上邽。

translations.literal: Wei, Grand General and Marquis of Pingxiang of Shu, had a descendant Ming who dwelt for generations at Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, Grand General and Marquis of Pingxiang of Shu, had a descendant Ming whose line made its home at Shanggui for generations.

translations.literal: The Jiang clan of Jiuzhen originally came from Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang clan of Jiuzhen traced its origins to Tianshui.

translations.literal: Two chancellors of the Jiang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Two members of the Jiang clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Ke and Gongfu.
translations.idiomatic: They were Ke and Gongfu.

translations.literal: The Lu clan derives from the Gui surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Lu clan traces its origin to the house of Gui.

sentences.zh: 田完裔孫齊宣王少子通，字季達，封於平原般縣陸鄉，即陸終故地，因以氏焉。

translations.literal: A descendant of Tian Wan, the youngest son of King Xuan of Qi, Tong, styled Jida, was enfeoffed at Luxiang in Ban County, Pingyuan—the former domain of Luzhong—and thereupon took it as the clan name.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant of Tian Wan, Tong, the youngest son of King Xuan of Qi, styled Jida, was enfeoffed at Luxiang in Ban County of Pingyuan—the ancient land of Luzhong—and took Lu as the clan name.

sentences.zh: 通謚曰元侯，生恭侯發，為齊上大夫。

translations.literal: Tong was posthumously titled Marquis Yuan and fathered Marquis Gong Fa, who was Senior Grand Master of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Tong was posthumously called Marquis Yuan; his son Fa, Marquis Gong, was Senior Grand Master of Qi.

translations.literal: Fa had two sons: Wan and Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Fa had two sons, Wan and Gao.

sentences.zh: 皐生邕，邕生漢太中大夫賈。

translations.literal: Gao fathered Yong; Yong fathered Jia, Grand Palace Counselor in Han.
translations.idiomatic: Gao's son Yong had a son Jia, Grand Palace Counselor under Han.

sentences.zh: 萬生烈，字伯元，吳令、豫章都尉，既卒，吳人思之，迎其喪，葬于胥屏亭，子孫遂為吳郡吳縣人。

translations.literal: Wan fathered Lie, styled Boyuan, Magistrate of Wu and Commandant of Yuzhang; after he died, the people of Wu missed him, welcomed his coffin, and buried him at Xuping Pavilion, and descendants thereupon became natives of Wu County, Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wan's son Lie, styled Boyuan, was Magistrate of Wu and Commandant of Yuzhang; when he died the people of Wu missed him, brought his coffin home, and buried him at Xuping Pavilion—and thereafter the clan were people of Wu County in Wu Commandery.

translations.literal: Two sons: Heng and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Heng and Xu.

translations.literal: Xu, styled Ziguang, was Magistrate of Xiangben.
translations.idiomatic: Xu, styled Ziguang, was Magistrate of Xiangben.

translations.literal: He fathered Hong, styled Shuluan, a staff officer of the native province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hong, styled Shuluan, was a staff officer of the native province.

sentences.zh: 鴻生建，字公榮，渤海太守。

translations.literal: Hong fathered Jian, styled Gongrong, Administrator of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's son Jian, styled Gongrong, was Administrator of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 建生曄，字奉光，本州從事。

translations.literal: Jian fathered Ye, styled Fengguang, a staff officer of the native province.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's son Ye, styled Fengguang, was a staff officer of the native province.

sentences.zh: 生恭，字彥祖，御史中丞、京兆尹。

translations.literal: He fathered Gong, styled Yanzu, Imperial Secretary and Intendant of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gong, styled Yanzu, was Imperial Secretary and Intendant of Jingzhao.

translations.literal: Gong fathered Huang, styled Gongbo.
translations.idiomatic: Gong's son Huang was styled Gongbo.

sentences.zh: 璜生文，字孝平，弘農都尉。

translations.literal: Huang fathered Wen, styled Xiaoping, Commandant of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Huang's son Wen, styled Xiaoping, was Commandant of Hongnong.

translations.literal: Wen fathered Qin, styled Gongdao, Magistrate of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Wen's son Qin, styled Gongdao, was Magistrate of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 親生衆，字世業，舉秀才，除郎中。

translations.literal: Qin fathered Zhong, styled Shiye, who was nominated as Outstanding Talent and appointed Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's son Zhong, styled Shiye, was nominated as Outstanding Talent and appointed Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 生賜，字思祖，丞相府主簿。

translations.literal: He fathered Ci, styled Sizu, Chief Clerk of the Chancellor's Office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ci, styled Sizu, was Chief Clerk of the Chancellor's Office.

sentences.zh: 生閎，字子春，潁川太守、尚書令。

translations.literal: He fathered Hong, styled Zichun, Administrator of Yingchuan and Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hong, styled Zichun, was Administrator of Yingchuan and Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

translations.literal: Three sons: Yang, Wen, and Huan, styled the Yingchuan Branch.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons—Yang, Wen, and Huan—called the Yingchuan Branch.

sentences.zh: 桓字叔文，生續，字知初，揚州別駕。

translations.literal: Huan, styled Shuwen, fathered Xu, styled Zhichu, Vice-Governor of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Huan, styled Shuwen, had a son Xu, styled Zhichu, Vice-Governor of Yang Province.

translations.literal: Three sons: Chou, Feng, and Bao, styled the Jingzhou Branch.
translations.idiomatic: Xu had three sons—Chou, Feng, and Bao—called the Jingzhou Branch.

translations.literal: Chou was Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Chou was Inspector of Jing Province.

translations.literal: Two sons: Su and Qian.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Su and Qian.

translations.literal: Su was Magistrate of Dantu and was styled the Dantu Branch.
translations.idiomatic: Su was Magistrate of Dantu; his line was called the Dantu Branch.

translations.literal: A tenth-generation descendant, Zhenzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Ten generations later came Zhenzhi.

sentences.zh: 揚州別駕續中子逢，漢尚書右僕射、樂安侯。

translations.literal: Feng, the middle son of Xu, Vice-Governor of Yang Province, was Vice Director of the Right in the Imperial Secretariat in Han and Marquis of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Feng, Xu's middle son and Vice-Governor of Yang Province, was Vice Director of the Right under Han and Marquis of Le'an.

sentences.zh: 五子：涉、表、瓊、昊、招，號樂安枝。

translations.literal: Five sons: She, Biao, Qiong, Hao, and Zhao, styled the Le'an Branch.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons—She, Biao, Qiong, Hao, and Zhao—called the Le'an Branch.

sentences.zh: 表生漢海鹽縣令穰，字子仁。

translations.literal: Biao fathered Rang, styled Ziren, Magistrate of Haiyan County in Han.
translations.idiomatic: Biao's son Rang, styled Ziren, was Magistrate of Haiyan County under Han.

translations.literal: He fathered Hui, Remonstrance and Counselor in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui was Remonstrance and Counselor in Jin.

sentences.zh: 恢生永興縣令弘，號諫議枝。

translations.literal: Hui fathered Hong, Magistrate of Yongxing County, styled the Remonstrance Branch.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's son Hong, Magistrate of Yongxing County, founded the Remonstrance Branch.

sentences.zh: 揚州別駕續少子褒，字叔明。

translations.literal: Bao, the youngest son of Xu, Vice-Governor of Yang Province, was styled Shuming.
translations.idiomatic: Bao, Xu's youngest son and Vice-Governor of Yang Province, was styled Shuming.

sentences.zh: 褒第三子紆，字叔盤，吳城門校尉。

translations.literal: Bao's third son Yu, styled Shupan, was Colonel of the Garrison Gate at Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's third son Yu, styled Shupan, was Colonel of the Garrison Gate at Wu.

translations.literal: Five sons: Dang, Yin, Sa, Yun, and Jun.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: Dang, Yin, Sa, Yun, and Jun.

sentences.zh: 駿字季才，九江都尉、太學博士。

translations.literal: Jun, styled Jicai, was Commandant of Jiujiang and Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, styled Jicai, was Commandant of Jiujiang and Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

translations.literal: Two sons: Xun and Mao.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Xun and Mao.

translations.literal: Mao, styled Zizhang, was Director of the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Mao, styled Zizhang, was Director of the Bureau of Appointments.

translations.literal: Six sons: Pang, Xi, Ying, Ying, Wei, and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons: Pang, Xi, Ying, Ying, Wei, and Yan.

sentences.zh: 穎第三子海隅縣令濯，生漢公。

translations.literal: Ying's third son, Zhuo, Magistrate of Haiyu County, fathered Hangong.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's third son Zhuo, Magistrate of Haiyu County, had a son Hangong.

translations.literal: Hangong fathered Lie.
translations.idiomatic: Hangong's son was Lie.

sentences.zh: 冽生晉本郡從事元之，隱居魚圻，號魚圻枝。

translations.literal: Lie fathered Yuanzhi, a staff officer of the native commandery in Jin, who retired to Yuqi and was styled the Yuqi Branch.
translations.idiomatic: Lie's son Yuanzhi was a staff officer in his native commandery under Jin; he retired to Yuqi, and his line was called the Yuqi Branch.

sentences.zh: 生英，字季子，長沙太守、高平相、員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He fathered Ying, styled Jizi, Administrator of Changsha, Chancellor of Gaoping, and Supernumerary Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ying, styled Jizi, was Administrator of Changsha, Chancellor of Gaoping, and Supernumerary Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.

translations.literal: Six sons: Shu, Ju, Ye, Wan, Cui, and Guan.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons: Shu, Ju, Ye, Wan, Cui, and Guan.

sentences.zh: 玩字士瑤，侍中、司空，贈太尉、興平康伯。

translations.literal: Wan, styled Shiyao, was Palace Attendant and Minister of Works and posthumously received the title Grand Commandant and Earl Kang of Xingping.
translations.idiomatic: Wan, styled Shiyao, served as Palace Attendant and Minister of Works and was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant and Earl Kang of Xingping.

sentences.zh: 六子：謐、儒、側、納、乂、始，號太尉枝。

translations.literal: Six sons: Mi, Ru, Ce, Na, Ai, and Shi, styled the Grand Commandant Branch.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons—Mi, Ru, Ce, Na, Ai, and Shi—called the Grand Commandant Branch.

sentences.zh: 始字祖興，五兵尚書、侍中。

translations.literal: Shi, styled Zuxing, was Director of the Bureau of War and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Shi, styled Zuxing, was Director of the Bureau of War and Palace Attendant.

translations.literal: Two sons: Chu and Wanzi.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Chu and Wanzi.

sentences.zh: 萬載，臨海太守、祕書監、侍中。

translations.literal: Wanzi was Administrator of Linhai, Director of the Imperial Library, and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Wanzi was Administrator of Linhai, Director of the Imperial Library, and Palace Attendant.

translations.literal: Four sons: Daowan, Shuyuan, Qun, and Zizhen.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Daowan, Shuyuan, Qun, and Zizhen.

sentences.zh: 子真字同宗，宋東陽太守。

translations.literal: Zizhen, styled Tongzong, was Administrator of Dongyang in Song.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhen, styled Tongzong, was Administrator of Dongyang under Song.

sentences.zh: 四子：惠曉、惠恭、惠徹、惠遠。

translations.literal: Four sons: Huixiao, Huigong, Huiche, and Huiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Huixiao, Huigong, Huiche, and Huiyuan.

sentences.zh: 惠徹字監，齊司徒府左曹掾。

translations.literal: Huiche, styled Jian, was a Clerk in the Left Section of the Chancellor's Office of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Huiche, styled Jian, was a Clerk in the Left Section of the Chancellor's Office under Qi.

translations.literal: Three sons: Guan, Xian, and Yin.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Guan, Xian, and Yin.

translations.literal: Xian, styled Xiaye, was Vice-Governor of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Xian, styled Xiaye, was Vice-Governor of Yang Province.

translations.literal: Four sons: Jue, Jiang, Wan, and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Jue, Jiang, Wan, and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 長沙太守英次子瓘，晉中書侍郎，號侍郎枝。

translations.literal: Guan, second son of Ying, Administrator of Changsha, was Vice Director of the Secretariat in Jin and was styled the Vice Director Branch.
translations.idiomatic: Guan, Ying's second son and Administrator of Changsha, was Vice Director of the Secretariat in Jin; his line was called the Vice Director Branch.

sentences.zh: 五世孫文盛，齊散騎常侍。

translations.literal: A fifth-generation descendant, Wensheng, was Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations later Wensheng was Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry under Qi.

sentences.zh: 生宣猛，字觀明，梁宣威將軍。

translations.literal: He fathered Xuanmeng, styled Guanming, General Who Displays Might of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuanmeng, styled Guanming, was General Who Displays Might under Liang.

sentences.zh: 宣猛生陳吏部侍郎潯，潯九世孫齊望。

translations.literal: Xuanmeng fathered Xun, Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel in Chen; nine generations after Xun came Qiwang.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmeng's son Xun was Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel in Chen; nine generations later came Qiwang.

translations.literal: Six chancellors of the Lu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Six members of the Lu clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: The Dantu Branch had Dunxin;
translations.idiomatic: The Dantu Branch produced Dunxin;

sentences.zh: 太尉枝有元方、象先、希聲；

translations.literal: the Grand Commandant Branch had Yuanfang, Xiangxian, and Xisheng;
translations.idiomatic: the Grand Commandant Branch produced Yuanfang, Xiangxian, and Xisheng;

translations.literal: the Vice Director Branch had Yi and Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: the Vice Director Branch produced Yi and Zhi.

translations.literal: The Zhao clan derives from the Ying surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao clan traces its origin to the house of Ying.

sentences.zh: 顓頊裔孫伯益，帝舜賜以嬴姓。

translations.literal: Boyi, a descendant of Zhuanxu, was granted the surname Ying by Emperor Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Boyi, a descendant of Zhuanxu, received the surname Ying from Emperor Shun.

sentences.zh: 十三世孫造父，周穆王封於趙城，因以為氏。

translations.literal: A thirteenth-generation descendant, Zaofu, was enfeoffed at Zhaocheng by King Mu of Zhou and thereupon took it as the clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen generations later Zaofu was enfeoffed at Zhaocheng by King Mu of Zhou and took Zhao as the clan name.

translations.literal: That place is Yong'an County in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: The site is Yong'an County in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 六世孫奄父，號公仲，生叔帶，去周仕晉文侯。

translations.literal: A sixth-generation descendant, Yanfu, styled Duke Zhong, fathered Shudai, who left Zhou to serve Marquis Wen of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Six generations later Yanfu, called Duke Zhong, had a son Shudai who left Zhou to serve Marquis Wen of Jin.

sentences.zh: 五世孫夙，晉獻公賜采邑於耿，河東皮氏縣有耿鄉是也。

translations.literal: A fifth-generation descendant, Su, was granted a fief at Geng by Duke Xian of Jin—the Geng Township in Pishi County, Hedong, was the site.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations later Su received a fief at Geng from Duke Xian of Jin—the site is Geng Township in Pishi County, Hedong.

sentences.zh: 夙生共孟，共孟生衰，字子餘，謚曰成季。

translations.literal: Su fathered Gongmeng; Gongmeng fathered Shuai, styled Ziyu, posthumously titled Lord Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Su's son Gongmeng had a son Shuai, styled Ziyu, posthumously called Lord Cheng.

sentences.zh: 成季十八世孫遷，為秦所滅，趙人立遷兄嘉為代王，後降於秦。

translations.literal: An eighteenth-generation descendant of Lord Cheng, Qian, was destroyed by Qin; the people of Zhao installed Qian's elder brother Jia as King of Dai, who later submitted to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen generations after Lord Cheng, Qian was wiped out by Qin; the Zhao people raised his elder brother Jia as King of Dai, but Jia later surrendered to Qin.

sentences.zh: 秦使嘉子公輔主西戎，西戎懷之，號曰趙王，世居隴西天水西縣。

translations.literal: Qin sent Jia's son Gongfu to command the Western Rong; the Western Rong embraced him and styled him King of Zhao; the line dwelt for generations at Xixian, Tianshui, Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Qin appointed Jia's son Gongfu to lead the Western Rong; they rallied to him and called him King of Zhao, and the clan settled for generations at Xixian in Tianshui, Longxi.

sentences.zh: 公輔十二世孫融，字長，後漢右扶風、大鴻臚。

translations.literal: A twelfth-generation descendant of Gongfu, Rong, styled Chang, was Governor of Right Fufeng and Grand Minister of Ceremonies in Later Han.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve generations after Gongfu, Rong, styled Chang, was Governor of Right Fufeng and Grand Minister of Ceremonies under the Later Han.

translations.literal: A seventh-generation descendant of Rong, Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Seven generations after Rong came Yao.

sentences.zh: 新安趙氏，後徙京兆奉天。

translations.literal: The Zhao clan of Xin'an later moved to Fengtian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao clan of Xin'an later relocated to Fengtian in Jingzhao.

translations.literal: The Zhao clan of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao clan of Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 南陽趙氏亦世居宛縣，後徒平原。

translations.literal: The Zhao clan of Nanyang also dwelt for generations at Wan County and later moved to Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao clan of Nanyang also lived for generations at Wan County before moving to Pingyuan.

translations.literal: Four chancellors of the Zhao clan.
translations.idiomatic: Four members of the Zhao clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Renben, Jing, Yanzhao, and Zongru.
translations.idiomatic: They were Renben, Jing, Yanzhao, and Zongru.

translations.literal: The Yan clan derives from the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan clan traces its origin to the house of Ji.

sentences.zh: 周武王封太伯曾孫仲弈於閻鄉，因以為氏。

translations.literal: King Wu of Zhou enfeoffed Taibo's great-grandson Zhongyi at Yanxiang, and they thereupon took it as the clan name.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu of Zhou enfeoffed Taibo's great-grandson Zhongyi at Yanxiang, and the clan took Yan as its surname.

sentences.zh: 又云，昭王少子生而手文曰「閻」，康王封於閻城。

translations.literal: Another account says that a younger son of King Zhao was born with the character "Yan" on his hand, and King Kang enfeoffed him at Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Another tradition holds that a younger son of King Zhao was born with the character "Yan" on his palm and that King Kang enfeoffed him at Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 又云，唐叔虞之後晉成公子懿，食采於閻邑，晉滅，子孫散處河洛，前漢末，居滎陽。

translations.literal: Another account says that Yi, a son of Duke Cheng of Jin, a descendant of Shuyu of Tang, received a fief at Yanyi; when Jin was destroyed, descendants scattered throughout the He and Luo region, and at the end of Former Han they dwelt at Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Another tradition says Yi, a son of Duke Cheng of Jin and descendant of Shuyu of Tang, held a fief at Yanyi; after Jin fell the clan scattered along the He and Luo rivers, and by the end of Former Han they lived at Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 尚書閻章生暢，侍中、北宜春侯。

translations.literal: Yan Zhang, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, fathered Chang, a Palace Attendant and Marquis of Beiyichun.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhang, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, had a son Chang, Palace Attendant and Marquis of Beiyichun.

translations.literal: Three sons: Xian, Jing, and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Xian, Jing, and Yan.

translations.literal: Xian was General of Chariots and Cavalry and Marquis of Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was General of Chariots and Cavalry and Marquis of Changshe.

sentences.zh: 顯生穆，避難徙于巴西之安漢。

translations.literal: Xian fathered Mu, who fled hardship and moved to Anhan in Baxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's son Mu fled calamity and relocated to Anhan in Baxi.

sentences.zh: 顯孫甫，魏武帝封為平樂鄉侯，復居河南新安。

translations.literal: Xian's grandson Fu was enfeoffed by Emperor Wu of Wei as Marquis of Pingle Township and again settled in Xin'an, Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's grandson Fu was made Marquis of Pingle Township by Emperor Wu of Wei and returned to Xin'an in Henan.

sentences.zh: 生牂柯太守璞，璞生晉殿中將軍、漢中太守讚。

translations.literal: He fathered Pu, Administrator of Zangke; Pu fathered Zan, General of the Palace in Jin and Administrator of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pu was Administrator of Zangke; Pu's son Zan was General of the Palace in Jin and Administrator of Hanzhong.

translations.literal: Zan fathered Heng, Administrator of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zan's son Heng was Administrator of Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 亨生北平太守安成亭侯鼎，字玉鉉，死劉聰之難。

translations.literal: Heng fathered Ding, Administrator of Beiping and Marquis of Ancheng Ting, styled Yuxuan, who died in the crisis of Liu Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Heng's son Ding, styled Yuxuan, was Administrator of Beiping and Marquis of Ancheng Ting and died in the turmoil of Liu Cong.

sentences.zh: 子昌，奔于代王猗盧，遂居馬邑。

translations.literal: His son Chang fled to Prince Yilu of Dai and thereupon settled at Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang fled to Prince Yilu of Dai and settled at Mayi.

sentences.zh: 孫滿，後魏諸曹大夫，自馬邑又徙河南。

translations.literal: A grandson, Man, was a Court Physician in Later Wei and moved again from Mayi to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Man was a Court Physician under Later Wei and moved from Mayi back to Henan.

sentences.zh: 孫善，龍驤將軍、雲中鎮將，因居雲州盛樂。

translations.literal: A grandson, Shan, was General of Dragon Cavalry and Garrison Commander of Yunzhong and settled at Shengle in Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Shan was General of Dragon Cavalry and Garrison Commander of Yunzhong and made his home at Shengle in Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 生車騎將軍、燉煌鎮都大將提，提生盛樂郡守進。

translations.literal: He fathered Ti, General of Chariots and Cavalry and Area Commander of Dunhuang; Ti fathered Jin, Administrator of Shengle Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ti was General of Chariots and Cavalry and Area Commander of Dunhuang; Ti's son Jin was Administrator of Shengle Commandery.

sentences.zh: 進少子慶，字仁度，後周小司空、上柱國、石保成公，賜姓大野氏，至隋復舊。

translations.literal: Jin's youngest son Qing, styled Rendu, was Junior Minister of Works in Later Zhou, Pillar of the State, and Duke of Baocheng of Shi, was granted the surname Daye, and under Sui the former surname was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's youngest son Qing, styled Rendu, was Junior Minister of Works under Later Zhou, Pillar of the State, and Duke of Baocheng of Shi; he received the surname Daye but reverted to Yan under Sui.

translations.literal: He fathered Pi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Pi.

translations.literal: One chancellor of the Yan clan.
translations.idiomatic: One member of the Yan clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Liben.
translations.idiomatic: He was Liben.

sentences.zh: 郝郝氏出自郝省氏，太昊之佐也。

translations.literal: The Hao clan derives from the Haosheng clan, assistants to Taihao.
translations.idiomatic: The Hao clan traces its origin to the Haosheng clan, aides to Taihao.

sentences.zh: 商帝乙之世，裔孫期封於太原之郝鄉，因以為氏。

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Yi of Shang, a descendant, Qi, was enfeoffed at Haoxiang in Taiyuan and thereupon took it as the clan name.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Emperor Yi of Shang, a descendant Qi was enfeoffed at Haoxiang in Taiyuan and took Hao as the clan name.

translations.literal: A descendant, Yan, was Senior Minister of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant Yan was Senior Minister of Qin.

translations.literal: Yan's grandson Yuan was Administrator of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's grandson Yuan was Administrator of Taiyuan.

translations.literal: He fathered Kui, General of the Household Who Subdues the Xiongnu in Han.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kui was General of the Household Who Subdues the Xiongnu under Han.

sentences.zh: 裔孫晉末因官徙潤州丹楊。

translations.literal: A descendant, at the end of Jin, moved to Danyang in Runzhou because of an office.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant relocated to Danyang in Runzhou on account of office at the end of Jin.

sentences.zh: 七世孫迴，自丹楊徙安陸。

translations.literal: A seventh-generation descendant, Hui, moved from Danyang to Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: Seven generations later Hui moved from Danyang to Anlu.

translations.literal: One chancellor of the Hao clan.
translations.idiomatic: One member of the Hao clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Chujun.
translations.idiomatic: He was Chujun.

translations.literal: The Xue clan derives from the Ren surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Xue clan traces its origin to the house of Ren.

sentences.zh: 黃帝孫顓頊少子陽封於任，十二世孫奚仲為夏車正，禹封為薛侯，其地魯國薛縣是也。

translations.literal: Yang, a younger son of Zhuanxu, grandson of the Yellow Emperor, was enfeoffed at Ren; a twelfth-generation descendant, Xizhong, was Director of Chariots under Xia; Yu enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xue—the place is Xue County in Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang, Zhuanxu's younger son and grandson of the Yellow Emperor, was enfeoffed at Ren; twelve generations later Xizhong was Director of Chariots under Xia, and Yu made him Marquis of Xue—at Xue County in Lu.

sentences.zh: 奚仲遷于邳，十二世孫仲虺，復居薛，為湯左相。

translations.literal: Xizhong moved to Pi; a twelfth-generation descendant, Zhonghui, again settled at Xue and was Left Chancellor to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhong moved to Pi; twelve generations later Zhonghui returned to Xue and served Tang as Left Chancellor.

translations.literal: Chen Hu and Zusi were both of this descent.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hu and Zusi both belonged to this line.

sentences.zh: 祖巳七世孫曰成，徙國於摯，更號摯國。

translations.literal: A seventh-generation descendant of Zusi, called Cheng, moved the state to Zhi and changed its name to the State of Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Seven generations after Zusi, Cheng moved the state to Zhi and renamed it the State of Zhi.

sentences.zh: 女大任，生周文王，至武王克商，復封為薛侯。

translations.literal: His daughter Tairen gave birth to King Wen of Zhou; when King Wu conquered Shang, he was again enfeoffed as Marquis of Xue.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter Tairen bore King Wen of Zhou; after King Wu conquered Shang, the line was again enfeoffed as Marquis of Xue.

sentences.zh: 齊桓霸諸侯，獨薛侯不從，黜為伯。

translations.literal: When Duke Huan of Qi dominated the feudal lords, the Marquis of Xue alone would not follow and was reduced to the rank of earl.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Huan of Qi dominated the feudal lords, the Marquis of Xue alone refused to follow and was demoted to earl.

sentences.zh: 歷三代，凡六十四世，其可記者：畛生初，初生厲侯陵，陵生宣武侯房，房生哀侯褒，褒生莊侯元，元生平侯貴，貴生昭侯直，直生襄侯夷，夷生桓侯辨，辨生康侯安興，安興生定公箱，箱生恭侯尚，尚生景侯魏，魏生宣侯伯勤，伯勤生簡侯文歡，文歡生惠侯夷黃，夷黃生靈侯英，英生文侯俱，俱生隱侯清，清生愍侯洪，為楚所滅。

translations.literal: Through three dynasties, for sixty-four generations in all, those who can be recorded: Zhen fathered Chu; Chu fathered Marquis Li Ling; Ling fathered Marquis Xuanwu Fang; Fang fathered Marquis Ai Bao; Bao fathered Marquis Zhuang Yuan; Yuan fathered Marquis Ping Gui; Gui fathered Marquis Zhao Zhi; Zhi fathered Marquis Xiang Yi; Yi fathered Marquis Huan Bian; Bian fathered Marquis Kang Anxing; Anxing fathered Duke Ding Xiang; Xiang fathered Marquis Gong Shang; Shang fathered Marquis Jing Wei; Wei fathered Marquis Xuan Boqin; Boqin fathered Marquis Jian Wenhuan; Wenhuan fathered Marquis Hui Yihuang; Yihuang fathered Marquis Ling Ying; Ying fathered Marquis Wen Ju; Ju fathered Marquis Yin Qing; Qing fathered Marquis Min Hong, who was destroyed by Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Across three dynasties the line ran for sixty-four recordable generations: Zhen to Chu to Marquis Li Ling to Marquis Xuanwu Fang to Marquis Ai Bao to Marquis Zhuang Yuan to Marquis Ping Gui to Marquis Zhao Zhi to Marquis Xiang Yi to Marquis Huan Bian to Marquis Kang Anxing to Duke Ding Xiang to Marquis Gong Shang to Marquis Jing Wei to Marquis Xuan Boqin to Marquis Jian Wenhuan to Marquis Hui Yihuang to Marquis Ling Ying to Marquis Wen Ju to Marquis Yin Qing to Marquis Min Hong—who was destroyed by Chu.

sentences.zh: 公子登仕楚懷王為沛公，不仕，隱於博徒，因以國為氏，所謂薛公也。

translations.literal: The prince's son Deng entered the service of King Huai of Chu as Duke of Pei; he did not serve and hid among gamblers, and thereupon took the state as his clan name—the so-called Duke of Xue.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's son Deng served King Huai of Chu as Duke of Pei, then withdrew, concealed himself among gamblers, and took the state's name as his clan—the so-called Duke of Xue.

sentences.zh: 生雲，雲生卬，卬生倪，為楚令尹。

translations.literal: He fathered Yun; Yun fathered Ang; Ang fathered Ni, who was Chief Minister of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Yun, whose son Ang had a son Ni, Chief Minister of Chu.

sentences.zh: 倪生翁，翁生鑒，漢初獻策滅黥布，封千戶侯。
