translations.literal: Ni fathered Weng; Weng fathered Jian, who at the beginning of Han offered a stratagem to destroy Qing Bu and was enfeoffed as a lord of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Ni's son Weng had a son Jian, who at the founding of Han proposed a plan to destroy Qing Bu and was enfeoffed as a lord of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 生瑑，瑑生茂宣，茂宣生懷則，懷則生引孫，引孫生廣德，字廣德，御史大夫。

translations.literal: He fathered Zhuan; Zhuan fathered Maoxuan; Maoxuan fathered Huaize; Huaize fathered Yinsun; Yinsun fathered Guangde, styled Guangde, Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His line ran through Zhuan, Maoxuan, Huaize, and Yinsun to Guangde, styled Guangde, Censor-in-Chief.

translations.literal: Guangde fathered Rao, Administrator of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Guangde's son Rao was Administrator of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 饒生愿，為淮陽太守，因徙居焉。

translations.literal: Rao fathered Yuan, who was Administrator of Huaiyang and thereupon moved there to dwell.
translations.idiomatic: Rao's son Yuan was Administrator of Huaiyang and moved his family there.

translations.literal: He fathered Fangqiu, styled Fuzi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fangqiu was styled Fuzi.

sentences.zh: 方丘生漢，字公子，後漢千乘太守。

translations.literal: Fangqiu fathered Han, styled Gongzi, Administrator of Qiancheng in Later Han.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqiu's son Han, styled Gongzi, was Administrator of Qiancheng under the Later Han.

sentences.zh: 漢生彪，字輔國，司徒祭酒。

translations.literal: Han fathered Biao, styled Fuguo, libationer of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Han's son Biao, styled Fuguo, was libationer of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 彪生侍御史安期，安期生中山相脩，脩生馬邑都尉山塗，山塗生山陽大守固，固生龍丘令文伯，文伯生東海相衍，衍生兗州別駕蘭，為曹操所殺。

translations.literal: Biao fathered Palace Attendant Anqi; Anqi fathered Zhongshan Chancellor Xiu; Xiu fathered Mayi Commandant Shantu; Shantu fathered Shanyang Administrator Gu; Gu fathered Longqiu Magistrate Wenbo; Wenbo fathered Donghai Chancellor Yan; Yan fathered Yanzhou Vice-Governor Lan, who was killed by Cao Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Biao's line ran through Palace Attendant Anqi, Zhongshan Chancellor Xiu, Mayi Commandant Shantu, Shanyang Administrator Gu, Longqiu Magistrate Wenbo, and Donghai Chancellor Yan to Yanzhou Vice-Governor Lan, who was killed by Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 子永，字茂長，從蜀先主入蜀，為蜀郡太守。

translations.literal: His son Yong, styled Maochang, followed Shu's founding lord into Shu and was Administrator of Shujun.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yong, styled Maochang, followed Shu's founding lord into Shu and became Administrator of Shujun.

sentences.zh: 永生齊，字夷甫，巴、蜀二郡太守，蜀亡，率戶五千降魏，拜光祿大夫，徙河東汾陰，世號蜀薛。

translations.literal: Yong fathered Qi, styled Yifu, Administrator of both Ba and Shu commanderies; when Shu fell, he led five thousand households in surrender to Wei, was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and moved to Fenyin in Hedong—the line was styled the Shu Xue for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's son Qi, styled Yifu, was Administrator of both Ba and Shu; when Shu fell he led five thousand households in surrender to Wei, was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, moved to Fenyin in Hedong, and the line came to be called the Shu Xue.

translations.literal: Two sons: Yi and Shi.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Yi and Shi.

sentences.zh: 懿字元伯，一名奉，北地太守，襲鄢陵侯。

translations.literal: Yi, styled Yuanbo, also called Feng, was Administrator of Beidi and inherited the Marquisate of Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, styled Yuanbo (also Feng), was Administrator of Beidi and inherited the marquisate of Yanling.

translations.literal: Three sons: Hui, Diao, and Xing.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Hui, Diao, and Xing.

sentences.zh: 恢一名開，河東太守，號「北祖」；

translations.literal: Hui, also called Kai, was Administrator of Hedong and was styled the "Northern Ancestor";
translations.idiomatic: Hui, also called Kai, was Administrator of Hedong and was known as the "Northern Ancestor";

translations.literal: Diao was styled the "Southern Ancestor";
translations.idiomatic: Diao was known as the "Southern Ancestor";

translations.literal: Xing was the "Western Ancestor."
translations.idiomatic: Xing was the "Western Ancestor."

sentences.zh: 雕生徒，徒六子：堂、暉、推、煥、渠、黃。

translations.literal: Diao fathered Tu; Tu had six sons: Tang, Hui, Tui, Huan, Qu, and Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Diao's son Tu had six sons: Tang, Hui, Tui, Huan, Qu, and Huang.

sentences.zh: 堂生廣，晉上黨太守，生安都。

translations.literal: Tang fathered Guang, Administrator of Shangdang in Jin, who fathered Andu.
translations.idiomatic: Tang's son Guang was Administrator of Shangdang in Jin and had a son Andu.

sentences.zh: 西祖興，字季達，晉河東太守、安邑莊公。

translations.literal: Xing, the Western Ancestor, styled Jida, was Administrator of Hedong in Jin and Duke Zhuang of Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: Xing the Western Ancestor, styled Jida, was Administrator of Hedong in Jin and Duke Zhuang of Anyi.

translations.literal: Three sons: Ge, Qing, and Tao.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Ge, Qing, and Tao.

sentences.zh: 濤字伯略，中書監，襲安邑忠惠公，與北祖、南祖分統部衆，世號「三薛都統」。

translations.literal: Tao, styled Bolue, was Director of the Secretariat, inherited Duke Zhonghui of Anyi, and with the Northern and Southern Ancestors divided command of the clansmen; for generations they were styled the "Three Xue Clan Chiefs."
translations.idiomatic: Tao, styled Bolue, was Director of the Secretariat, inherited Duke Zhonghui of Anyi, and with the Northern and Southern Ancestors divided command of the clansmen—the line for generations was called the "Three Xue Clan Chiefs."

translations.literal: Three sons: Qiang, Yi, and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Qiang, Yi, and Qing.

sentences.zh: 彊字公偉，秦大司徒、馮翊宣公。

translations.literal: Qiang, styled Gongwei, was Grand Minister of Revenue of Former Qin and Duke Xuan of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang, styled Gongwei, was Grand Minister of Revenue of Former Qin and Duke Xuan of Fengyi.

translations.literal: Three sons: Bian, Yong, and Chong.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Bian, Yong, and Chong.

sentences.zh: 辯字元伯，後魏雍州刺史、汾陰武侯。

translations.literal: Bian, styled Yuanbo, was Inspector of Yongzhou in Later Wei and Marquis Wu of Fenyin.
translations.idiomatic: Bian, styled Yuanbo, was Inspector of Yongzhou under Later Wei and Marquis Wu of Fenyin.

sentences.zh: 生謹，字法慎，內都坐大官、涪陵元公。

translations.literal: He fathered Jin, styled Fashen, Chief Provisioner of the Inner Court and Duke Yuan of Fuling.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jin, styled Fashen, was Chief Provisioner of the Inner Court and Duke Yuan of Fuling.

sentences.zh: 五子：洪祚、洪隆、瑚、昂、積善，號「五房」，亦為瀵上五門薛氏大房。

translations.literal: Five sons: Hongzuo, Honglong, Hu, Ang, and Jishan, styled the "Five Houses," also called the Great House of the Five Gates Xue clan above the Fen.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons—Hongzuo, Honglong, Hu, Ang, and Jishan—called the "Five Houses," also known as the principal branch of the Five Gates Xue clan above the Fen River.

sentences.zh: 薛氏定著二房：一曰南祖，二曰西祖。

translations.literal: The recorded clans of the Xue clan are two houses: first the Southern Ancestor, second the Western Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: The Xue clan's registered branches are two: the Southern Ancestor and the Western Ancestor.

translations.literal: Three chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Three members of the clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: The Southern Ancestor had Ne;
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Ancestor branch produced Ne;

translations.literal: the Western Ancestor had Ji and Yuanchao.
translations.idiomatic: the Western Ancestor branch produced Ji and Yuanchao.
